newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Prime keen on acquisition in 1997.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Prime keen on acquisition in 1997.

text.p: Regional television broadcaster Prime Television Ltd said on Thursday it was keen on making an acquisition in the 1997 calendar year, which could be either locally or overseas.

"I like to think that we would be able to make some acquisitions in this calendar year," Prime chief executive George Brown told reporters after Prime reported its first half results for the 1996/97 year ending June 30.
"We are very keen to buy a radio asset in regional Australia. We see it as a natural fit to our business," Brown said. He said Prime was also looking overseas for purchases.
"We have looked at everything through Asia, North and South America, we shall continue to look there," Brown said.
Brown said Prime would prefer to move into a country where it could be an operator of a television network.
"But, whatever we do overseas, we will do with a local partner," he said. Prime earlier reported a 21.7 percent rise in net profit to A$7.98 million in the six months ended December 31.
Prime also reported a jump in long-term borrowing to A$140 million in the six month period from A$75 million a year earlier.
Prime's debt levels rose after its purchased Western Australia television network Golden West Network late last year.
Brown also advocated a relaxation in Australia's cross-media ownership rules, which are currently being reviewed by the government.
"I can't see the logic in overseas investors to acquire those assets, as they can now, at the expense of someone like ourselves," Brown said.
He said he saw a lot of synergy between television and radio in the same geographical market. Prime operates television networks in regional New South Wales and Victoria.
At 1.00 p.m. (0200 GMT), Prime shares were steady at A$2.50 giving it a market capitalisation of A$222.51 million.
